newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra signs A$3bln bank-syndicated debt facility.
newsitem.headline: Telstra signs A$3bln bank-syndicated debt facility.

text.p: Australian state-owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp on Friday signed its previously announced A$3 billion syndicated bank loan, said to be the largest ever arranged in the country.
The previously announced facility comprises two tranches: a A$1 billion, 364-day facility and a A$2 billion five-year facility, Telstra said.
The funds will replenish working capital after Telstra recently paid the government a special dividend of A$3 billion.
The dividend brought Telstra's capital structure into line with relevant peer group standards before partial privatisation, the company said. The dividend is to be banked this year.
The government plans to sell a third of Teltra in calendar 1997, raising an estimated A$8 billion.
The loan syndication closed substantially oversubscribed on May 12, Telstra said.
"Banks were required to commit either A$300 million, A$200 million or A$100 million to the transaction and all participants were scaled back on final allocation," it said.

"The facility is structured to provide pricing and flexibility which will enable Telstra to refinance in the capital markets at an appropriate time and as opportunities arise," Telstra group managing director for finance Paul Rizzo said in a statement.
